AMM.title: Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM)
AMM.description: The AMM provides detailed maintenance procedures, servicing instructions, and troubleshooting guides for all aircraft systems. It is the primary reference for line and base maintenance activities.

ATA21.description: The air conditioning system uses engine bleed air processed through air cycle machines (packs) to provide pressurized, temperature-controlled air to the cabin and cockpit. The system includes dual packs, a mixer unit, and zone temperature controllers.
inspection_procedure: 1. Verify pack valve operation using ECAM system page
2. Check bleed air duct integrity for leaks using soap solution
3. Inspect pack flow control valve actuator
4. Verify zone temperature controller calibration
5. Check cabin pressure controller operation
6. Inspect recirculation fan filters and replace if contaminated
7. Record findings in technical log

ATA24.description: The electrical power system generates, distributes, and manages 115V AC and 28V DC power throughout the aircraft. It includes engine-driven generators, APU generator, transformer rectifier units, and emergency battery systems.
inspection_procedure: 1. Check generator output voltage and frequency under load
2. Inspect generator control unit (GCU) parameters
3. Test bus tie contactors operation
4. Verify transformer rectifier unit output
5. Check battery charge status and electrolyte level
6. Test emergency power transfer sequence
7. Inspect wiring harness for chafing and damage

ATA27.description: The A320 fly-by-wire flight control system uses electronic computers to translate pilot inputs into control surface movements. The system includes ailerons, elevators, rudder, spoilers, slats, and flaps managed by flight control computers (ELAC, SEC, FAC).
inspection_procedure: 1. Perform flight control computer self-test via MCDU
2. Check all control surface travel limits and free play
3. Inspect actuator attachment fittings and bearings
4. Verify sidestick transducer calibration
5. Test autopilot servo engagement and disengagement
6. Inspect flap and slat track assemblies for wear
7. Check spoiler symmetry during ground test

ATA29.description: The triple hydraulic system (Green, Blue, Yellow) provides 3000 PSI pressure for flight controls, landing gear, brakes, thrust reversers, and cargo doors. The Green system is engine-driven, Blue is electrically driven, and Yellow has both engine-driven and electric backup pumps.
inspection_procedure: 1. Check hydraulic reservoir fluid levels for all three systems
2. Inspect hydraulic lines and fittings for leaks
3. Verify system pressure readings (nominal 3000 PSI)
4. Test hydraulic pump output flow rate
5. Check accumulator pre-charge pressure
6. Inspect hydraulic filters and replace if differential pressure exceeded
7. Test emergency hand pump operation (Yellow system)
8. Verify Power Transfer Unit (PTU) operation

ATA32.description: The retractable tricycle landing gear includes dual-wheel nose gear and four-wheel main gear bogies. The system features oleo-pneumatic shock absorbers, carbon disc brakes with anti-skid protection, and auto-brake systems.
inspection_procedure: 1. Check tire pressures and tread depth
2. Inspect brake wear indicators on all wheel assemblies
3. Check oleo strut pressure and extension
4. Inspect landing gear door actuators and hinges
5. Verify wheel speed transducer operation
6. Test anti-skid system function
7. Inspect gear retraction mechanism and uplocks
8. Check nose wheel steering actuator

ATA36.description: The pneumatic system distributes engine bleed air for air conditioning, pressurization, wing and engine anti-ice, hydraulic reservoir pressurization, and cross-engine starting.
inspection_procedure: 1. Check bleed valve operation and response time
2. Inspect precooler and fan air valve
3. Verify bleed air temperature and pressure
4. Leak test pneumatic ducting using pressure decay method
5. Check crossbleed valve operation
6. Inspect high-pressure ground connection fitting
7. Verify overpressure relief valve function

ATA49.description: The Honeywell APS3200 APU provides electrical power and bleed air on the ground and in flight up to 20,000 ft. It enables engine starting without external ground power and provides backup electrical generation.
inspection_procedure: 1. Check APU oil level and condition
2. Inspect APU inlet and exhaust for FOD damage
3. Verify APU start sequence timing parameters
4. Check EGT values during start and steady-state operation
5. Test APU generator load sharing capability
6. Inspect APU fire detection and extinguishing systems
7. Check APU bleed valve operation

ATA52.description: Aircraft door systems include passenger doors, service doors, cargo doors, and emergency exits. Each door features integrated escape slides, pressure seals, and mechanical lock indicators.
inspection_procedure: 1. Inspect door seal condition and compression
2. Check door hinge and pivot bearings
3. Verify door assist mechanism (power assist / manual)
4. Test door warning system (ECAM indications)
5. Inspect escape slide container and pressure gauge
6. Check gust lock mechanism operation
7. Verify cargo door latch and lock indicators

ATA71.description: The A320 is powered by two CFM56-5B series turbofan engines. Each engine produces approximately 27,000 lbs of thrust and drives hydraulic pumps, electrical generators, and bleed air systems.
inspection_procedure: 1. Perform borescope inspection of hot section (combustion chamber, HPT)
2. Check engine oil quantity and magnetic chip detector
3. Inspect fan blades for FOD damage and erosion
4. Verify engine vibration levels (N1, N2)
5. Check EGT margins and trend monitoring data
6. Inspect engine cowlings, latches, and hinges
7. Test thrust reverser deployment and stow
8. Check fuel nozzle spray pattern

FIM.title: Fault Isolation Manual (FIM)
FIM.description: The FIM provides systematic troubleshooting procedures to isolate faults indicated by ECAM warnings, maintenance messages, and reported defects.

isolation_steps: 1. Check GCU BITE codes via MCDU
2. Measure generator output voltage
3. Check IDG oil temperature and pressure
4. Inspect wiring harness between generator and GCU
5. If GCU codes present, replace GCU per AMM 24-21-11
6. If IDG oil pressure low, disconnect IDG per AMM 24-11-02

2. Measure individual cell voltages
3. Check battery temperature
4. Test battery charger output
5. If cell voltage below 1.8V, replace battery per AMM 24-31-01

2. Inspect pump case drain flow
3. Visual inspection of hydraulic lines for leaks
4. Check system pressure with engine running
5. If leak found, identify location and repair per SRM
6. If pump output low, replace pump per AMM 29-11-01

2. Check EGT trend data for gradual or sudden increase
3. Perform fuel nozzle flow check
4. Borescope HPT blades for damage
5. If FADEC codes present, replace EGT probe per AMM 71-31-01
6. If blade damage found, contact engine OEM for repair limits

IPC.title: Illustrated Parts Catalogue (IPC)
IPC.description: The IPC provides part numbers, quantities, and assembly breakdown for all aircraft components. Used for ordering replacement parts and verifying correct installation.

SRM.title: Structural Repair Manual (SRM)
SRM.description: The SRM provides allowable damage limits and repair procedures for aircraft structural components including fuselage skin, wings, empennage, and doors.

damage_limits.repair_procedure: Blend out scratches within limits. If exceeded, apply doubler patch per SRM 51-70-11.
Any crack in pressurized fuselage skin requires immediate repair per SRM 53-00-06. Dents within limits may be left unrepaired with monitoring.

WDM.title: Wiring Diagram Manual (WDM)
WDM.description: The WDM provides schematic wiring diagrams for all aircraft electrical circuits. Used for fault isolation, modification embodiment, and wire routing verification.

diagrams.title: AC Generator 1 Circuit
diagrams.description: Shows wiring from Engine 1 IDG through GCU to AC Bus 1. Includes current transformers, voltage regulators, and bus tie relay circuits.

CMM.title: Component Maintenance Manual (CMM)
CMM.description: The CMM provides detailed overhaul, repair, and test procedures for individual components removed from the aircraft. Used by component repair shops.

ALS.title: Airworthiness Limitations Section (ALS)
ALS.description: The ALS defines mandatory maintenance tasks and structural inspection intervals that cannot be exceeded. These are regulatory requirements established by the aircraft type certificate.

structural_inspections.affected_area: Wing Station 200 to 400, lower skin panels
Aft pressure bulkhead, all radial seams

MPD.title: Maintenance Planning Document (MPD)
MPD.description: The MPD defines the scheduled maintenance program including task intervals, check packages (A/B/C/D checks), and zonal inspection requirements.

tasks: General visual inspection of aircraft exterior
Engine oil level check and replenishment
Detailed structural inspection of fuselage, wings, empennage
Full functional test of all systems

scheduled_tasks.description: Landing gear tire pressure check and brake wear measurement
Engine oil quantity check and magnetic chip detector inspection
APU oil level check and inlet inspection
